description: Puts screens on the design canvas of one of the user's Better Design projects, as editable frames. The owner sees them when they open the canvas, and can then move, resize and retype every layer by hand. Use it for four jobs. A user journey: one step for each screen of the flow, in order, with the happy path first and its loading, empty and error states under it in the same step; take the steps from the feature map when the repository has one, and give each frame the `next` frames it leads to, so the canvas draws the flow's arrows. Design options: one step for each option, so they sit side by side. Component usage: one step for each screen that uses the component. States: one step, with every state of one screen. Send the real screen. For a web screen, render it, then pass its HTML with the CSS it needs in a <style> block; the canvas draws boxes, text, borders, radii, shadows, pictures and inline SVG. For a SwiftUI screen when no Mac is at hand, send its source as swift: the canvas reads the code and draws it as editable layers, close to an iPhone but not exact. For a SwiftUI or UIKit screen on a Mac, run it in the iOS simulator, take `xcrun simctl io <simulator id> screenshot --type=jpeg shot.jpg`, read `axe describe-ui --udid <simulator id>`, and send both as native. The canvas shows the screenshot exactly, with every element in the tree as a layer the person can select. Its text is part of the picture, so it cannot be retyped. One call takes up to 24 frames. Call again for a longer flow.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

height.description: Only for a screen that fills its window, such as one with a bar fixed to the bottom: the window height in pixels. Left out, the frame is as tall as its content.

html.description: A web screen as HTML that carries its own CSS in a <style> block or inline styles. No script runs and nothing loads from the network. Send exactly one of html, native or swift.

name.description: The frame's name on the canvas, such as "Cart, loading".

native.description: A SwiftUI or UIKit screen as the iOS simulator shows it, sent in place of html. screenshot: the simulator's screenshot as a data URL, such as data:image/jpeg;base64,... tree: the JSON `axe describe-ui --udid <simulator id>` prints for the same screen. The frame takes the screen's size in points, so leave width and height out.

next.description: The names of the frames in this call that this one leads to, such as ["Payment"]. The canvas draws an arrow to each one, as a prototype does.

step.description: The column this frame sits in. Frames with the same step stack top to bottom, and steps run left to right in the order they first appear.

swift.description: A SwiftUI screen as source code, for an agent with no Mac and no simulator, sent in place of html. Send the view's code: a `struct ... : View` with its `body`, or only the views inside the body. The canvas reads it as text, runs none of it, and draws each view as a layer a person can edit, close to how an iPhone shows it but not pixel exact. It reads VStack, HStack, ZStack, Spacer, Text, Image(systemName:), Button, Toggle, Label, List, Section, NavigationStack, ScrollView, shapes, colours, the Better Design kit views such as DSButton, and the common modifiers: padding, frame, font, fontWeight, foregroundStyle, background, cornerRadius, clipShape, opacity, shadow. Anything else draws as a box named "Not drawn: ...". The screen is 393 by 852 points unless width and height say otherwise.

width.description: The width to render at, in pixels. Defaults to 1440 for html and 393 points for swift. Use 390 for a phone screen in html.

projectId.description: The id of the project whose canvas to draw on, from create-design-system or the address of the project page.

title.description: What this drawing shows, such as "Checkout flow".

name: draw-on-canvas
title: Draw Screens on the Canvas
